days.title: Arrival in Tokyo
days.tagline: Touch down at Narita. Neon lights and konbini runs await.
highlights: 18:30 — Land at Narita Airport
Narita Express to Shibuya — 75 min, ¥3,250
Buy Suica IC cards at the airport kiosk
Check into hotel. Light konbini dinner — onigiri is your new best friend
days.food: Konbini onigiri — umeboshi, kombu fillings are naturally GF + vegan. Available 24/7.
days.tip: Withdraw yen at 7-Eleven ATMs — best rates, English menus. Japan runs on cash.

days.title: TeamLab & Harajuku
days.tagline: Immersive digital art, then the sensory overload of Shibuya at night.
highlights: TeamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills — ¥3,800, book 2 months ahead
Meiji Shrine — ancient forest in the heart of the city
Harajuku & Takeshita Street — pop culture, fashion, chaos
Shibuya Crossing at dusk — you live here. Golden Gai after dark.

activities.name: Dinner — Ain Soph Journey (vegan, GF options)

transport.note: All within central Tokyo, use Suica

days.food: Ain Soph Journey (Shinjuku) — fully vegan, GF options. Afuri ramen in Harajuku — ask for tamari.
days.tip: Wear dark clothing at TeamLab — projections look best on black. Book tickets the moment they open (2 months ahead).

days.title: Kamakura
days.tagline: 13th-century capital. Giant Buddha, ocean temples, island at sunset.
highlights: JR Yokosuka Line from Shibuya — 60 min, ¥940
Tsurugaoka Hachimangū shrine → Komachi-dōri street
Kōtoku-in — the Great Buddha, 13m tall, cast in 1252
Hase-dera Temple — ocean views, hydrangeas in May
Enoden train to Enoshima Island — caves, shrine, panoramic views
days.food: Bowls Kamakura (plant-based café near Hase). Look for vegetable tempura sets (note: batter has gluten).
days.tip: Time your visit to catch golden hour at Enoshima observation tower.

days.title: Mt Fuji
days.tagline: The iconic pagoda-and-peak view. Fuji is famously shy — go early.
highlights: Highway bus from Shibuya → Kawaguchiko — 2 hrs, ¥2,200
Chureito Pagoda — 398 steps to THE photo. Best light before noon.
Kawaguchiko Ropeway to Mt Tenjō — panoramic Fuji + lake view
Walk the north shore of Lake Kawaguchi — Fuji reflected in water
days.food: Limited veg/GF options around Kawaguchiko. Bring snacks from Tokyo. Rice dishes at lakeside restaurants.
days.tip: Clouds roll in by midday almost daily. The early bus is non-negotiable.

days.title: Tokyo → Kumamoto
days.tagline: A quick flight south. By lunch, you're in Kyushu.
highlights: Flight: Haneda → Kumamoto — 1h50, arrive by lunch
Limousine bus from Shibuya to Haneda (30 min, ¥1,300)
Kumamoto Castle — rebuilt after 2016 earthquake, stunning stone walls
Shimotori covered arcade — Kumamoto's beating heart
Whole afternoon free to explore — way more time than the 6hr shinkansen
days.food: Kumamoto is famous for horse meat (basashi) — not for you, but the veggie izakayas near Shimotori are excellent. Try tofu steak sets.
days.tip: Book HND→KMJ flight early — ANA Super Value or JAL Special Saver can drop to ¥8,000–12,000 if booked 75+ days ahead.

days.title: Mt Aso & Bike Ride
days.tagline: Active volcano, vast caldera, then e-bikes through landscapes most tourists never see.
highlights: JR Hōhi Line → Aso Station — 75 min through mountains
Morning: Bokuya Rides guided e-bike through protected grasslands
Rolling hills, volcanic panoramas, thrilling downhill return
Afternoon: Nakadake Crater — steaming vents, turquoise lake (if accessible)
Kusasenri — vast green meadows inside the caldera
days.food: Limited veggie options in Aso area. Bring snacks from Kumamoto konbini. Rice-bowl restaurants for GF.
days.tip: Book Bokuya Rides at asocalderatourism.com. Start with the ride while legs are fresh. Helmets provided.

days.title: Kurokawa Onsen
days.tagline: Mountain onsen village. Soak in open-air baths hidden among cedar forests.
highlights: Bus from Kumamoto Sakuramachi → Kurokawa Onsen — 2.5 hrs through mountains
Rotenburo meguri — wooden pass (¥1,500) for 3 outdoor baths of your choice
Wander the village: cedar-lined paths, stone bridges, steam rising everywhere
Each ryokan has a unique bath — forest views, river-side, cave, rock formations
Evening return to Kumamoto — or linger for golden hour at the village

activities.name: Arrive Kurokawa, buy Nyuto Tegata pass
Village walk — bridges, steam, cedar paths

days.food: Limited options in Kurokawa. Tofu Kissho for handmade tofu dishes (vegan-friendly, soy sauce contains wheat — bring tamari). Pack snacks from Kumamoto konbini.
days.tip: Rotenburo meguri pass works at 28 participating ryokan baths. Bring a small towel (or buy one). Onsen etiquette: wash before entering, no swimwear, tattoos usually OK in Kurokawa.

days.title: Kumamoto → Onomichi
days.tagline: Shinkansen north. A hillside port town of cats, temples, and sea views.
highlights: Kumamoto → Hakata → Fukuyama → Onomichi — 3.5 hrs total
Optional: 2-hr Hiroshima Peace Memorial detour en route
Senkoji Ropeway — hilltop park overlooking the Seto Inland Sea
Cat Alley (Neko no Hosomichi) — narrow paths with feline street art
Reserve bikes at Onomichi terminal for tomorrow's Shimanami Kaido
days.food: Onomichi ramen is the local specialty (not veggie-friendly). Try Komichi Café near Cat Alley for lighter fare.
days.tip: If you can spare 2 hrs, detour to Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park en route. It's one of the most powerful experiences in Japan.

days.title: Shimanami Kaido → Osaka
days.tagline: 70 km across 6 islands. Then straight to Japan's kitchen.
highlights: 06:30 — Send bags via takkyubin to Osaka hotel (~¥2,500/bag)
07:00 — Pick up e-bikes, ferry to Mukaishima
Ride across 6 islands — soaring bridges, Seto Inland Sea blue
Stop at Setoda, Omishima shrines, beaches along the way
~15:00 — Drop bikes at Imabari terminal
Imabari → Okayama → Shin-Osaka — train ~3.5 hrs. Arrive ~19:00.

activities.name: Send bags via takkyubin
activities.note: per bag, arrives next day at Osaka hotel

activities.name: Pick up e-bikes at Onomichi terminal
Arrive Osaka, check into Namba hotel

transport.note: Ride Onomichi → Imabari (70km), then train to Osaka

days.food: Pack snacks before starting. Setoda has Dolce gelato shop. Omishima has mikan everything. Konbini stops on islands.
days.tip: Takkyubin: drop bags at any konbini or Yamato office by morning. Follow the blue line on the road. E-bikes worth every yen.

days.title: Osaka — Dōtonbori & Shinsekai
days.tagline: Neon canals, retro towers, and the art of eating till you drop.
highlights: Sleep in — your legs deserve it after yesterday
Dōtonbori — the neon-lit canal, Glico Running Man sign
Shinsekai — retro district under Tsutenkaku Tower
Street food crawl — takoyaki, okonomiyaki, yakiimo
Hozenji Yokocho at dusk — stone-paved alley, tiny restaurants

activities.name: Late start — rest day for legs

days.food: Paprika Shokudo Vegan (Namba). Green Earth (Shinsaibashi). For GF okonomiyaki, ask 'kome-ko de dekimasu ka?' (rice flour?).
days.tip: Osaka's motto is kuidaore — eat till you drop. Dōtonbori at night is pure electricity.

days.title: Osaka — Castle & Markets
days.tagline: Castle parks, market stalls, and the city that never stops eating.
highlights: Osaka Castle — 8-story keep, panoramic city views, ¥600
Walk through Castle Park — beautiful in mid-May greenery
Kuromon Market — 'Osaka's Kitchen', browse 170+ stalls
Shinsaibashi arcade — covered shopping stretching for blocks
days.food: Kuromon Market — look for fresh fruit, pickles, rice dishes. Mochi (glutinous rice ≠ gluten!) is naturally GF.
days.tip: Kuromon Market before 2pm — stalls close early. Supermarket bento after 7pm is 30-50% off.

days.title: Kyoto
days.tagline: Thousands of torii gates. Gold temples. Bamboo forests. Geisha at dusk.
highlights: JR Special Rapid to Kyoto — 30 min, ¥580
Fushimi Inari — go before 9am. Thousands of vermillion gates.
Kinkaku-ji — gold-leaf temple reflected in mirror pond
Arashiyama Bamboo Grove → Tenryū-ji → Togetsukyo Bridge
Gion at dusk — traditional machiya, geiko quarter
days.food: Kyoto has the best vegan scene in Japan. Shigetsu at Tenryū-ji (shōjin ryōri, ¥3,300–5,500). Mumokuteki Café. Falafel Garden (Gion).
days.tip: Fushimi Inari at dawn is life-changing. The first tunnel of gates, almost empty, almost holy.

days.title: Osaka → Tokyo
days.tagline: Final bullet train. Choose your Tokyo finale.
highlights: Morning: last Osaka stroll — pick up any remaining omiyage
Shinkansen Shin-Osaka → Tokyo — 2h45, ¥13,870
Option A: Asakusa — Sensō-ji, Tokyo's oldest temple
Option B: Akihabara — electronics, anime, retro gaming
Farewell dinner — Golden Gai or Michelin-star shōjin ryōri
days.food: Daigo near Shiba Park — 2-Michelin-star Buddhist vegan. Book ahead. Or casual Golden Gai.
days.tip: For a special last meal: Daigo is extraordinary. Otherwise, kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) — kappa, avocado, inari are veggie.

days.title: Departure
days.tagline: One last Tokyo morning. Then Narita. Then memories.
highlights: Tsukiji Outer Market — breakfast stalls, tamagoyaki, fresh fruit
Last shopping — Tokyo Station omiyage shops are incredible
Japanese Kit-Kats, matcha sweets, furoshiki wrapping cloths
19:00 — Narita Express to airport
22:50 — ✈️ Fly home to Warsaw. Sayonara, Japan.
days.food: Stock up on snacks at Narita — excellent selection. Senbei (rice crackers, GF!), mochi, regional KitKats.
days.tip: Tax-free shopping: ¥5,000+ at participating stores = ~10% savings. Don't open sealed items before leaving Japan.

Do you have tamari soy sauce?

japanesePhrases.meaning: Please make dashi without bonito flakes

safeFoods: Onigiri (rice balls) — umeboshi, kombu, nattō fillings
Mochi — glutinous rice ≠ gluten, naturally GF
watchOut: Soy sauce (shōyu) contains wheat → request tamari
Dashi broth usually made with bonito (fish) → ask for kombu dashi
Miso soup often has bonito dashi

jrPassAnalysis.recommendation: Definitely buy individual tickets. With Tokyo→Kumamoto now a flight, your shinkansen legs are only Kumamoto→Onomichi (¥13,000) and Osaka→Tokyo (¥13,870) plus local trains. The 7-day pass (¥50,000) costs more than your actual train spend. Individual tickets + Nozomi access is the clear winner.
jrPassAnalysis.note: No JR Pass needed. Individual shinkansen tickets can be booked at JR ticket counters (midori no madoguchi) or via SmartEX app.

transport.suicaCard: Buy at airport kiosk. ¥2,000 (¥500 deposit + ¥1,500 balance). Works on all metro, JR local, buses, konbini payments.

takkyubin.what: Luggage forwarding service — send bags between hotels
takkyubin.how: Drop at any konbini (7-Eleven, FamilyMart) or Yamato Transport office

bookings.note: At JR ticket counters (midori no madoguchi)

domesticFlight.note: HND → KMJ one-way (¥8,000–20,000 depending on booking lead time)

trains.note: Shinkansen Kumamoto→Onomichi + Osaka→Tokyo + local trains (no Tokyo→Kumamoto shinkansen)

hotels.note: 13 nights across 5 stays (Kumamoto +1, Osaka -1) ÷ 2 people per room

kurokawa.note: Kurokawa Onsen day trip: bus RT ¥5,000 + rotenburo pass ¥1,500 + lunch

budget.note: Excludes international flights. Includes domestic HND→KMJ flight. Mid-range estimates. 2 hotel rooms for 4 people.

packing: Light rain jacket — May has sudden showers
Layers — Mt Aso highlands are cooler
Small towel — many restrooms lack hand dryers
Allergy/dietary card in Japanese (print before trip)
Minimal luggage — lots of stairs and tight trains
Coin purse — Japan uses more coins than expected

travels.details: WAW → NRT, landing 18:30. Then Narita Express to Shibuya (75 min).
Day trip. Return via Enoden + JR same evening.
06:30 departure, return ~17:00. Through mountain roads with Fuji views.
HND → KMJ. Morning flight, arrive by lunch. Way faster than 6hr shinkansen.
Day trip. Through dramatic mountain valleys. Then e-bike tour at Aso.
Day trip. Through mountain roads to the hidden onsen village. Return same evening.
Kumamoto → Hakata (40 min) → Fukuyama (1h30) → local to Onomichi (20 min).
Ferry to Mukaishima, then 6 bridges across 6 islands. The ride of a lifetime.
Drop bikes at Imabari terminal → train across Seto bridge → Shin-Osaka → Namba.
Day trip. Quick JR ride, packed day of temples and shrines.
Nozomi — fastest bullet train. Views of Mt Fuji from the right side if you're lucky.
Narita Express from Tokyo Station (60 min, ¥3,250). Flight 22:50.

hotels.budget: Up to €250/night per room (2 rooms needed)
hotels.note: Prices are approximate per room per night in May 2026. Book early for best rates. All hotels can receive takkyubin luggage.

restaurants.note: Curated for vegetarian/vegan travelers with celiac-level gluten allergy. GF = gluten-free. Always carry a Japanese allergy card and tamari packets.
restaurants.allergyCardJp: 私はセリアック病です。小麦・大麦・ライ麦を食べられません。醤油の代わりにたまりを使ってください。
restaurants.allergyCardEn: I have celiac disease. I cannot eat wheat, barley, or rye. Please use tamari instead of soy sauce.
safeFoods: Onigiri — umeboshi, kombu, nattō fillings (check labels for wheat)
Yakiimo — roasted sweet potato from street vendors
Fresh fruit — Japan's fruit is extraordinary
Tofu (hiyayakko/yudofu) — ask for tamari instead of soy sauce
dangerFoods: Soy sauce (shōyu) — contains wheat. Request tamari.
Ramen/udon/soba noodles — wheat (soba is buckwheat + wheat mix)
Dashi broth — usually bonito (fish), ask for kombu dashi
Okonomiyaki — wheat batter unless rice flour specified

spots.name: Ain Soph Journey
spots.nameJp: アインソフ ジャーニー
spots.mustTry: Vegan pancakes — over half the menu is GF
spots.note: English GF menu. Cross-contact possible in shared kitchen. 1 min from Shinjuku-sanchōme C5 exit.

spots.name: Vegan Izakaya Masaka
spots.nameJp: ヴィーガン居酒屋マサカ
spots.mustTry: Vegan karaage with teriyaki mayo
spots.note: All items vegan. QR code English menu. Small (20 seats), arrive early on weekends.

spots.name: Vegan Bistro Jangara

spots.mustTry: Vegan ramen with GF noodle swap (small upcharge)
spots.note: Fully vegan. Dedicated GF noodle option. 3 min from Harajuku Station.

spots.name: Brown Rice Cafe
spots.mustTry: Seasonal vegan set meal (shoku teishoku)
spots.note: Hidden inside Neal's Yard Remedies shop. Walk through the shop, glass door in back. 1 min from Omotesandō A1.

spots.name: Tera Cafe
spots.mustTry: Seasonal shōjin set — served by monks (Wed–Fri)
spots.note: Temple food, no garlic/onion. GF possible with advance notice — soy sauce contains wheat. Ask for tamari.

spots.name: Magokoro (Kamakura)
spots.mustTry: Magokoro set: brown rice, tofu 'meat', tempeh, 3 daily sides
spots.note: Yuigahama beach views. Farm-to-table. Fri–Sun only. 4 min from Hase Station. Perfect for Day 3 Kamakura trip.

spots.name: Choice Kitchen (Kawaguchiko)
spots.mustTry: 40–50 dish vegetable buffet with local Yamanashi produce
spots.note: 15 min walk from Kawaguchiko Station. Lunch & dinner buffet. Perfect for Day 4 Mt Fuji trip.

kumamoto.label: Kumamoto & Kyushu

spots.name: Cafe Pony
spots.mustTry: Vegan plant-based burger with brown rice
spots.note: Your SAFEST option in Kumamoto. Explicit GF + vegan menu. Macrobiotic focus. 13 min walk from Heisei Station.

spots.name: Purely Restaurant
spots.nameJp: ピュアリィレストラン
spots.mustTry: Monthly rotating organic kaiseki with zero-pesticide rice
spots.note: Beautiful 140-year house. Contact ahead (+81-96-323-1552) for GF protocols — not a dedicated GF kitchen.

spots.name: Tofu Kissho (Kurokawa Onsen)
spots.mustTry: Agedashi tofu, dengaku (miso-glazed), tofu ice cream
spots.note: Charming thatched-roof tofu shop. Vegan-friendly but miso contains wheat — NOT celiac-safe without tamari. Bring your own GF soy sauce.

kumamoto.survivalTips: Kumamoto is rural — GF options are genuinely limited. Stock up at konbini: plain onigiri (ume/kombu), edamame, fresh fruit, yakiimo. For Kurokawa day trip, pack snacks from Kumamoto.

spots.name: Komedoko Shokudo
spots.mustTry: Vegan GF ramen with rice flour noodles — your best bet in Onomichi
spots.note: Owner actively develops GF dishes. Waterfront views. Request advance notice for GF prep. This is the one reliable option.

spots.name: Kameyama Goya (Innoshima Island)
spots.mustTry: Green curry (verify no fish sauce) or pho with vegetable broth
spots.note: Only real island restaurant option. Confirm GF and ask about fish sauce in curries. Scenic cycling café stop.

whatToPack: Onigiri from Onomichi konbini (grab 4-5 before starting)
Individual tamari packets (for any rice dishes you find)
cyclingFuelGuide.konbiniStops: Lawson/FamilyMart/7-Eleven every 15-20km along route. Safe bets: rice balls (check for wheat - 小麦), edamame, bananas, Pocari Sweat.
cyclingFuelGuide.tip: Use Google Translate camera mode to scan konbini labels for 小麦 (wheat). Kanji is your friend.

spots.name: Vegan and Gluten Free Osaka
spots.nameJp: ビーガンアンドグルテンフリーオオサカ
spots.mustTry: Everything — ALL menu items are vegan AND gluten-free
spots.note: 100% dedicated GF + vegan facility. 3 min from JR Osaka Station (B1F Ekimae 4th Building). Reservations recommended. Your safest meal in Osaka.

spots.name: OKO Fun Okonomiyaki
spots.mustTry: Vegan okonomiyaki with okara (soy pulp) batter instead of wheat
spots.note: Separate grill for GF orders. The Osaka experience you NEED — okonomiyaki without the wheat.

spots.name: Pivot BASE Cafe
spots.nameJp: ピボットベースカフェ
spots.mustTry: Vegan takoyaki (¥1,000 for 10 pieces)
spots.note: 100% vegan. Takoyaki has wheat flour — NOT GF. Okonomiyaki can be made GF on request. English menu.

spots.name: CHIBO Diversity
spots.nameJp: ちぼ ダイバーシティ
spots.mustTry: Vegan donburi or shōjin ryōri plate
spots.note: Clearly labeled menus for GF/vegan/halal/shōjin. Staff trained on allergies. Right on Dotonbori main drag.

spots.name: Choice Cafe
spots.mustTry: Grain & bean burger with salad (¥1,100)
spots.note: Uses TAMARI throughout (not regular soy sauce). Broth without fish. Best celiac-safe option in Kyoto. Closed Thursdays.

spots.name: Gion Soy Milk Ramen
spots.nameJp: 祇園豆乳ラーメン うのゆきこ
spots.mustTry: Soy Milk Snow Ramen with rice flour noodles (¥1,500)
spots.note: 100% plant-based. Rice flour noodles (GF). Tamari used. Weekday lunch only (11–14:00). World's only soy milk patissier.

spots.name: Shigetsu at Tenryū-ji
spots.mustTry: Multi-course shōjin set (¥3,300–¥8,000) in temple garden
spots.note: RESERVATION REQUIRED (075-882-9725). Michelin recognized. Inside Tenryū-ji Temple (¥500 garden entry). Standard soy sauce — request tamari at booking (not guaranteed).

spots.name: Kyoto Engine Ramen
spots.nameJp: 京都エンジンラーメン
spots.mustTry: Kyoto Beaning Vegan Ramen (edamame-based, ¥1,800) + GF noodles (+¥200)
spots.note: In-house broth = wheat-free. GF noodles available. Two vegan options. Safest ramen in Kyoto for celiac.

spots.name: Ain Soph Journey Kyoto
spots.nameJp: アインソフ ジャーニー京都
spots.mustTry: Matcha pancakes (¥1,800) or cutlet burger
spots.note: GF + Oriental Vegan options. Kitchen not allergen-free — cross-contamination possible. 2 min from Hankyu Kawaramachi exit 9.
